entities.name: Acathius
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Acathius (died c. 250) was a Christian bishop of Melitene (modern Malatya in eastern Turkey) who was martyred during the early Roman persecutions of Christianity. Venerated as a saint in both the Catholic and Orthodox traditions, he is one of the numerous early bishops who died rather than apostatise, contributing to the foundational martyrological culture that shaped Christian identity in the pre-Constantinian era.

Melitene was an important Roman military and administrative centre in eastern Cappadocia, strategically positioned near the Euphrates frontier with the Parthian and later Sassanid empires. Its Christian community is attested from an early period, and Acathius's episcopate fell during the years of localised and sometimes intense Roman persecution of Christian communities before the Constantinian peace.

The details of Acathius's martyrdom are preserved in hagiographic tradition that presents him as dying with exceptional courage and faith. His inclusion in the Roman and Greek martyrologies reflects the early Church's systematic commemoration of bishops who died for their faith as exemplars of Christian commitment. His feast day is celebrated in both traditions, and he contributes to the extensive catalogue of martyred bishops from Asia Minor that populated early Christian sacred geography.
